title: Engagement maximization
abstract: We investigate the management of information provision to maximize user engagement. A principal sequentially reveals signals to an agent who has a limited amount of information processing capacity and can choose to exit at any time. We identify a “dilution” strategy—sending rare but highly informative signals—that maximizes user engagement. The platform's engagement metric shapes the direction and magnitude of biases in provided information relative to a user‐optimal benchmark. Even without intertemporal commitment, the platform replicates full‐commitment revenue by inducing the user's belief to remain “as uncertain as” the prior until the rare, decisive signal arrives and induces stopping. We apply our results to two contexts: an ad‐supported internet media platform and a teacher attempting to engage test‐motivated students.
abstract_zh: 我们研究了如何管理信息提供以最大化用户参与度。一位委托人向具有有限信息处理能力且可随时选择退出的代理人顺序揭示信号。我们识别出一种“稀释”策略——发送罕见但信息量大的信号——以最大化用户参与度。平台的参与度指标决定了所提供信息相对于用户最优基准的偏差方向与幅度。即使缺乏跨期承诺能力，平台也能通过使用户信念保持“与先验一样不确定”，直到罕见的关键信号出现并引发停止行为，从而复制完全承诺下的收益。我们将研究结果应用于两个场景：广告支持的互联网媒体平台，以及试图吸引考试驱动型学生的教师。

title: Comparative Cantillon effects in the Canadian and Australian art markets
title_zh: 加拿大与澳大利亚艺术市场的比较康替龙效应
authors: Douglas J. Hodgson, Cameron M. Weber, Bronwyn Coate
abstract: Abstract As far back as 1755, Richard Cantillon analyzed how changes in the money supply affected relative prices in the economy. In times of monetary infusion, prices of certain types of goods and services could be expected to rise, depending upon the initial distribution of the money and therefore initial spending. Cantillon emphasized the case of new money falling into the hands of wealthy agents, driving up spending on luxuries, such as artworks (as well as financial assets), and causing their relative prices to increase. We present new evidence on the “Cantillon effect” as a potential explanation for movements in the prices of Canadian and Australian paintings since the mid‐1970s. We econometrically analyze the relationship between time series of the money supply and art prices in each country. Both countries represent peripheral art markets dominated by domestic private and corporate collectors, and they should thus be more responsive to domestic rather than international economic and monetary conditions. For both markets, we distinguish and separately analyze different tiers of the market, separating the very top from a lower segment. We find that prices for top Canadian artists follow the money supply relatively well over the long term, with a similar but slightly weaker result for the top Australian segment; notably, Australian middlebrow prices move more in line with the Consumer Price Index. These results suggest that national art markets are not homogeneous and that segmenting them for analytical purposes may be useful. Specifically, we find stronger evidence of a Cantillon effect in the upper end of the market, while prices of lower‐prestige paintings move more in line with consumer goods prices.
abstract_zh: 早在1755年，理查德·坎蒂隆就分析了货币供给变化如何影响经济中的相对价格。在货币注入时期，某些商品和服务的价格预计会上涨，具体取决于货币的初始分配及由此产生的初始支出。坎蒂隆强调，当新增货币落入富裕阶层手中时，会推高奢侈品（如艺术品及金融资产）的支出，导致其相对价格上升。我们提供了关于“坎蒂隆效应”的新证据，将其作为自20世纪70年代中期以来加拿大和澳大利亚绘画价格变动的潜在解释。我们运用计量经济学方法，分析了各国货币供给时间序列与艺术品价格之间的关系。这两个国家均属于由国内私人及企业收藏家主导的边缘艺术市场，因此它们对国内而非国际经济与货币状况的反应更为敏感。针对这两个市场，我们区分并分别分析了不同市场层级，将顶级市场与较低层级市场分开。研究发现，长期来看，加拿大顶级艺术家的价格与货币供给的走势相对吻合，澳大利亚顶级市场的结果类似但略弱；值得注意的是，澳大利亚中端市场价格与消费者价格指数的变动更为一致。这些结果表明，国家艺术市场并非同质化，按分析目的对其进行分层可能具有价值。具体而言，我们在市场高端发现了更强的坎蒂隆效应证据，而低声望画作的价格则更贴近消费品价格的变动。

title: Climate and Prehistoric Migration
authors: Peter Huybers, Marco Tabellini, Charles A. Taylor, Francesco Toti
official: 官方在线 2026-06-22 · 来源：出版社网页
abstract: What factors drove human migration before modern states, markets, and borders? We develop a sorting framework in which climate-specific subsistence knowledge depreciates with ecological distance. To test this, we use ancient DNA identity-by-descent segments to construct bilateral migration flows across Western Eurasia over the last 10,000 years. We document three main findings. First, migration flows decline with differences in growing degree days, precipitation, and soil characteristics between origins and destinations. Second, the binding factor varies across subsistence systems: farmers exhibit strong thermal and soil matching, while pastoralists match most strongly on precipitation. Third, periods of warming increase farmer expansion while cooling increases pastoral expansion in patterns that recover known archaeological migration episodes. Migration also acts as a margin of climate adaptation: populations exposed to temperature change move to destinations that partly offset the shift.

title: The Central Bank’s Dilemma: Look Through Supply Shocks or Control Inflation Expectations?
title_zh: 央行的两难困境：忽视供给冲击还是控制通胀预期？
authors: Paul Beaudry & Thomas J Carter & Amartya Lahiri
official: 官方在线 2026-05-15 · 来源：出版社网页
abstract: When countries are hit by supply shocks, central banks often face the dilemma of either looking through such shocks or reacting to them to ensure that inflation expectations remain anchored. In this paper, we propose a tractable framework to capture this dilemma and explore optimal policy under various assumptions on how agents form their expectations and the sophistication with which those expectations account for the central bank’s announced policies. While our analysis covers a wide range of potential specifications, our baseline results focus on level-k thinking (LKT) – a form of bounded rationality that enjoys significant support in the experimental literature and encompasses both adaptive expectations (AE) and rational expectations (RE) as special cases. Nonetheless, we show that the optimal policy under LKT is qualitatively very different from its analogues under AE and RE, exhibiting abrupt pivots in the policy stance. In particular, it is optimal for the central bank to initially look through supply shocks until a threshold is reached, then pivot discontinuously to a more hawkish anti-inflationary stance. We find that such pivots can, if optimally executed, be compatible with soft landings in the sense that most (or even all) of the reduction in inflation occurs through re-anchoring of expectations rather than economic slack. We also discuss risks and why policy errors in terms of tightening too late or too slowly can be especially costly in such an environment.

title: Loose bricks in the wall: Underground press and political opposition in non-democracies
title_zh: 墙上的松动砖块：非民主国家的地下媒体与政治反对
abstract: Abstract This study utilizes locations of underground publications, known as samizdat , to analyze the impact of access to political knowledge on shaping institutional change in the German Democratic Republic during 1989–1990. Survival analysis reveals that regions with greater underground press activity were significantly more likely to experience protests following the fall of the Berlin Wall on November 9, 1989. This delay can be attributed to the increased repression of dissent. However, support for regime change did not necessarily translate into support for rapid German reunification, as evidenced by the voting results of the 1990 democratic elections. Although samizdat did not appear to coordinate the initial protests, it played an informational role in shaping preferences toward gradual institutional change. Finally, in addition to its information function, underground press activities were instrumental in forming opposition that challenged the non-democratic regime, thereby determining the onset of democratization.

title: Essentiality of degree r in cooperative games with transferable utility
title_zh: 可转移效用合作博弈中度r的必要性
abstract: Abstract Cooperative game theory has proposed different notions of powerful players. For example, big-boss games (Muto et al. 1988) and clan games (Potters et al. 1989) are particular cases of veto games (Bahel 2016). The present paper extends these veto games by assuming that there is a given subset of powerful (or essential) players, but only a few (as opposed to all) essential players are required for a coalition to have a positive group value. The resulting games, which are called r -essential games, encompass convex games (Shapley 1971) and veto games. We show that r -essential games have a nonempty core. We give a recursive description of the core. Moreover, it is shown that the core and the bargaining set are equivalent for r -essential games. An application to networks is provided.
